facts.statement: The genus Bobbodus was described by Zangerl in 1981.
Bobbodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalians that lived during the Carboniferous and Permian periods.
facts.quote: Bobbodus is an extinct genus of eugeneodont holocephalian from the Carboniferous and Permian periods.

facts.statement: Bobbodus lived from the Kasimovian to the Wuchiapingian stages, between 307 and 254.14 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kasimovian to Wuchiapingian (307 to 254.14 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type species, Bobbodus schaefferi, is known from three specimens found on the ancient eastern coast of the Panthalassic Ocean.
facts.quote: B. schaefferi is the type species and is known from three specimens, all from what was the eastern coast of the Panthalassic Ocean.

facts.statement: Fossils of Bobbodus schaefferi have been found in the Kasimovian of Iowa, the Gzhelian of Nebraska, and the Asselian of Kansas.
facts.quote: Fossils of this species were found in the Kasimovian of Iowa, Gzhelian of Nebraska, Asselian of Kansas.

facts.statement: Specimens of Bobbodus schaefferi include partial upper and lower teeth, the palatoquadrate, and the gill arch.
facts.quote: Specimens of this species show the partial upper and lower dentition, the palatoquadrate, and gill arch.

facts.statement: Bobbodus belongs to the family Eugeneodontidae.
Bobbodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: The second species, Bobbodus xerxesi, is known from a single tooth found in Wuchiapingian-aged deposits in the Baghuk Mountains of central Iran.
rejected.quote: A second species, B. xerxesi, is known from a single tooth found in Wuchiapingian-aged deposits in the Baghuk Mountains of central Iran.
